# Tukey test {#sec-tukey}

{{< include ../preamble.qmd >}}

## Concepts and intuitions {.unnumbered}

## Formal {.unnumbered}

$$
    q_s = \frac{|Y_A - Y_B|}{ \hat{\sigma}/ \sqrt{n}}
$${#eq-tukey}

## Examples {.unnumbered}


Before running a Tukey HSD test, we first need to fit an Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) model. Once the model is fitted, we apply the `TukeyHSD()` function to evaluate pairwise differences between the groups.

```{r}
#| echo: true

# 1. Load the built-in PlantGrowth dataset
data("PlantGrowth")

# 2. Fit an ANOVA model (weight as a function of the treatment group)
aov_model <- aov(weight ~ group, data = PlantGrowth)

# 3. Run the Tukey HSD post hoc test
tukey_results <- TukeyHSD(aov_model)

# 4. View the numerical results
print(tukey_results)
```


```{r}
#| echo: true

# Adjust plotting margins so the y-axis labels (group comparisons) aren't cut off
par(mar = c(5, 6, 4, 2) + 0.1)

# Plot the Tukey HSD results
# 'las = 1' ensures the y-axis labels are horizontal and easy to read
plot(tukey_results, las = 1, col = "darkred")
```


## Visualizing with a Boxplot and Significance Letters

To display the distribution of the data alongside the statistical results, a boxplot is standard practice. We can use base R's `boxplot()` and `text()` functions to draw the graph and manually apply our significance letters above each group.

```{r}
#| echo: true

# 1. Create the base R boxplot
# We explicitly set 'ylim' to extend the y-axis so the letters don't get cut off
boxplot(weight ~ group, data = PlantGrowth,
        main = "Plant Weight by Treatment Group",
        xlab = "Treatment Group",
        ylab = "Dried Weight",
        col = c("lightblue", "mistyrose", "lightgreen"),
        ylim = c(3, 7.5))

# 2. Define the significance letters based on the Tukey HSD output
# The order must match the boxplot groups: ctrl, trt1, trt2
sig_letters <- c("ab", "a", "b")

# 3. Calculate the maximum value for each group to correctly position the letters
# tapply applies the max() function to 'weight', grouped by 'group'
max_weights <- tapply(PlantGrowth$weight, PlantGrowth$group, max)

# 4. Add the letters to the plot
# x = 1:3 corresponds to the x-axis positions of the three boxes
# y = max_weights + 0.2 places the text just above the highest data point (whisker)
text(x = 1:3,
     y = max_weights + 0.2,
     labels = sig_letters,
     col = "darkred",
     cex = 1.2,     # Increases text size
     font = 2)      # Makes the text bold
```


### Automating Significance Letters with `multcompView`

Instead of manually determining which group gets an "a" or "b", we can use the `multcompLetters4()` function from the `multcompView` package.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# 1. Install (if necessary) and load the package
# install.packages("multcompView")
library(multcompView)

# (Assuming aov_model and tukey_results are already generated from the first step)
# aov_model <- aov(weight ~ group, data = PlantGrowth)
# tukey_results <- TukeyHSD(aov_model)

# 2. Generate the letters automatically
# multcompLetters4 requires both the ANOVA model and the Tukey results
cld <- multcompLetters4(aov_model, tukey_results)

# 3. Extract the letters specifically for our 'group' variable
auto_letters <- cld$group$Letters

# 4. CRITICAL STEP: Reorder the letters to match the boxplot's x-axis!
# Base R boxplots order the x-axis by factor levels (ctrl, trt1, trt2).
# However, multcompLetters4 defaults to ordering groups by descending mean values.
# We must re-sort our letters vector to match the plot's order.
ordered_letters <- auto_letters[levels(PlantGrowth$group)]

# 5. Plot exactly as before, but using our automated, ordered letters
boxplot(weight ~ group, data = PlantGrowth,
        main = "Plant Weight by Treatment Group (Automated Letters)",
        xlab = "Treatment Group",
        ylab = "Dried Weight",
        col = c("lightblue", "mistyrose", "lightgreen"),
        ylim = c(3, 7.5))

# Calculate max weights for positioning
max_weights <- tapply(PlantGrowth$weight, PlantGrowth$group, max)

# Overlay the automated letters
text(x = 1:3,
     y = max_weights + 0.2,
     labels = ordered_letters,
     col = "darkred",
     cex = 1.2,
     font = 2)
```

### A Quick Note on the Code:
* **`multcompLetters4()`**: This is the workhorse function. It needs both the original `aov()` object and the `TukeyHSD()` object to run correctly.
* **Reordering**: Step 4 is the most common trap people fall into. If you don't re-align the names of the letters with the factor levels of your data, R will apply the right letters to the wrong boxes on your graph. Subsetting by `levels(PlantGrowth$group)` forces the letters into the exact order the boxplot expects.
